audits.title: Lessons learned from transfusion audits.
audits.standard: Self-inspection forms approved by the hospital transfusion committee (indication, consent, immunohaematology tests, documentation)
audits.setting: Six hospital facilities, German Red Cross Blood Donor Service North-East
audits.other_findings: Informed consent was most often inadequate; a documentation checklist is recommended.
audits.citation: Moog R. Lessons learned from transfusion audits. Transfus Apher Sci. 2016;54(3):377-379. doi:10.1016/j.transci.2015.11.017. PMID: 26928918.

audits.title: Wrong-Patient Blood Transfusion Error: Leveraging Technology to Overcome Human Error in Intraoperative Blood Component Administration.
audits.standard: Documentation of patient identification: two electronic signatures, transfusion start and stop times and volume transfused
audits.intervention: Bedside barcode transfusion verification in four phases and Epic anaesthesia information management system documentation with automated audit reports.
audits.other_findings: Pre-Epic shortfall mainly reflected missing paper blood component requisitions.

Wrong-Patient Blood Transfusion Error: Leveraging Technology to Overcome Human Error in Intraoperative Blood Component Administration. audits.title: Audit and education: Role in safe transfusion practice.
audits.standard: Complete blood request form fields (second identifier, diagnosis, haematology, component, transfusion history, urgency, signatures)

cycle1.result: 91.42% of request forms incomplete; incomplete second identification 91.03%.

audits.intervention: Series of CMEs on safe transfusion practice for clinicians and staff from 1 August 2014.
audits.other_findings: 6894 forms in total; phlebotomist signature still missing in 45.19% in December.
audits.citation: Patidar GK, Kaur D. Audit and education: Role in safe transfusion practice. Asian J Transfus Sci. 2018;12(2):141-145. doi:10.4103/ajts.ajts_135_17. PMID: 30692799.

audits.title: Improving Documentation Quality of Blood Transfusion Request Forms: A Two-Cycle Quality Improvement Initiative at a Tertiary Hospital in Sudan.
audits.standard: International transfusion request documentation standards (not named in abstract)

cycle1.result: Deficiencies identified (baseline figures not reported in abstract).

audits.intervention: Standardised transfusion request form with staff training (PDSA).

cycle2.result: Date of birth 35 (87.8%); file number 39 (97.6%); current Hb 40 (100%); indication 33 (82.9%); collector signature 39 (97.6%); collection date/time 39 (97.6%).

audits.other_findings: Number of units requested declined slightly to 34 (85.4%). Abstract gives the second-cycle n as both 42 and 40.

Improving Documentation Quality of Blood Transfusion Request Forms: A Two-Cycle Quality Improvement Initiative at a Tertiary Hospital in Sudan. Cureus. 2025;17(10):e94553. doi:10.7759/cureus.94553. PMID: 41246730.

audits.title: Clinical Audit of Transfusion Safety and Monitoring at Al-Kareemat Specialized Complex, Sudan: A Two-Cycle Quality Improvement Study.
audits.standard: WHO-aligned bedside transfusion safety, monitoring and haemovigilance criteria (eight criteria)
audits.setting: Al-Kareemat Specialized Complex for Clinics and Inpatient Care

cycle1.result: Patient identification 96.8% (213/220); 15-minute observation 69.5% (153/220); end-of-transfusion vital signs 80.9% (178/220); haemovigilance reporting of suspected reactions 33.3% (2/6).

audits.intervention: Targeted quality improvement package of staff reinforcement and standardised monitoring and reporting documentation.

cycle2.result: 15-minute observation 90.0% (108/120); end-of-transfusion vital signs 91.7% (110/120); haemovigilance reporting 100.0% (3/3).

audits.other_findings: Suspected transfusion reactions were similar across cycles (2.7% vs 2.5%).
audits.citation: Hamed SAH, Ibrahim AIM, Ali ZAM, Ahmed Abdelghani AA, Ahmed RA, Taha STI, et al.. Clinical Audit of Transfusion Safety and Monitoring at Al-Kareemat Specialized Complex, Sudan: A Two-Cycle Quality Improvement Study. Cureus. 2026;18(2):e102769. doi:10.7759/cureus.102769. PMID: 41783885.

audits.title: Prospective audit of blood transfusion request forms and continuing medical education to optimise compliance of clinicians in a hospital setting.
audits.standard: Complete and correct entries on blood requisition forms
audits.setting: Department of Transfusion Medicine, Jaypee Hospital, tertiary care centre

cycle1.result: 45.77% of blood requisition form entries were complete and correct; 23.45% of incomplete entries came from emergency and trauma.

audits.intervention: Continuing medical education for clinicians on transfusion request details.

cycle2.result: 76.75% of entries were complete and correct; cumulative mean score rose from 20687 to 30870.

audits.other_findings: After CME, obstetrics and gynaecology generated the most incomplete entries (35.09%).
audits.citation: Pandey P, Setya D, Mirza SM, Singh MK. Prospective audit of blood transfusion request forms and continuing medical education to optimise compliance of clinicians in a hospital setting. Transfus Med. 2021;31(1):16-23. doi:10.1111/tme.12722. PMID: 33000508.
